risk_note: RV2 attribution task (orders module): implements the application services of contract CT-24l (adminApproveClaimItem / adminRejectClaimItem), transcribing 08 BR-ATTR-20 / 30 / 32 without changing any attribution outcome; per orchestrator ruling J-1 neither route is mounted and the contract stays planned (mounting is a later task, needing the settlement port, snapshot wiring and the result notification). In one transaction: the pipeline's lockOrderKey first, the order re-read FOR UPDATE, then every affected claims row locked in ascending id. Already attributed → the item closes itself (same applicant cancelled, otherwise rejected NOT_IN_POOL), 200, no order write; VOID → system ORDER_INVALID with decided_by empty, on approve and on reject (the agent's chosen code and reason kept in the audit); other pending items on the same sub-order → NOT_IN_POOL, each claim summarised and announced; a decided item or stale row_version → 20902 claim_item; reject takes only the six agent codes; reason 5–200 characters into claims.reason and the audit. On approval orders writes only user_id, user_basis=claim, source columns / paid_at_source when empty (as the sync path) and order_status_history (field rebate, source claim); locked and rebate_status R3 belong to settlement through the declared port rebate.onClaimApproved, called inside the lock with the pre-write snapshot (the production placeholder rejects, so approval cannot go live before settlement). Commission snapshot and source backfill run as in the pipeline; claim.resolved is enqueued in the transaction. The claim intake path now takes the same order locks (ascending, after the user lock) before reading attribution, so an intake racing an approval cannot leave a pending item behind (Codex r1 S1). Rule tests (56, [AC-B1-10k#n]) written by Codex in two runs (the second only fixed the kit's pgboss.job query shape), red before the implementation; implementation by an Opus 5.5 subagent in two runs.
